column1: # The on-screen gamepad's layouts (dm/android/overlay_layout.h hit-tests them; gfx_vk_present.c draws the app's theme on them): the ergonomic layout of the
# "Themed Virtual Controllers" designs, written by devtools/theme_render.py --layout from themes/ergo (every theme shares it). Two layouts, the same controls in the
# same order in each: tablet (designed at 1216x760) and phone (915x412); the app takes the one nearer its window's aspect (overlay_layout.h OV_PHONE_ASPECT).
# A game profile's android.tsv moves single controls with `overlay <layout> <name> <x> <y>`; dm/android/tools/android_profile.py compiles the result into
#   name     what android.tsv and a theme's theme.tsv call the control
#   kind     stick_l, stick_r, button, dpad (its four directions, and the diagonals between them), menu (the menu button: pauses the game and opens the settings; always shown)
#   anchor   where x is measured from: 0 the window's left edge, 0.5 its middle, 1 its right edge (a thumb reaches as far from the edge on any width)
#   x        the centre's offset from the anchor, in window heights
#   y        the centre, as a fraction of the window's height
#   w, h     the size, in window heights (w = h: a round control)
#   button   the DM_BTN_* bit a button sends, - for the others
#   label    the text the theme-less drawing puts on a button, ~ for none
